claim: Collectively migrating epithelia feature both nematic (p = 2) and hexatic (p = 6) orders.
source: we demonstrate that collectively migrating epithelia feature both nematic (i.e. p = 2) and hexatic (i.e. p = 6) orders, with the former being dominant at large and the latter at small length scales.
evidence: This claim is supported by the hydrodynamic theory developed in the manuscript and validated against cell-resolved models.

claim: Nematic order is dominant at large length scales in epithelia.
source: we demonstrate that collectively migrating epithelia feature both nematic (i.e. p = 2) and hexatic (i.e. p = 6) orders, with the former being dominant at large and the latter at small length scales.
evidence: The manuscript presents theoretical predictions and numerical simulations showing nematic dominance at large scales.

claim: Hexatic order is dominant at small length scales in epithelia.
source: we demonstrate that collectively migrating epithelia feature both nematic (i.e. p = 2) and hexatic (i.e. p = 6) orders, with the former being dominant at large and the latter at small length scales.
evidence: The manuscript presents theoretical predictions and numerical simulations showing hexatic dominance at small scales.

claim: The structure factor of epithelia exhibits two different power-law scaling regimes.
source: Such a remarkable multiscale liquid crystal order leaves a distinct signature in the system's structure factor, which exhibits two different power-law scaling regimes, reflecting both the hexagonal geometry of small cells clusters and the uniaxial structure of the global cellular flow.
evidence: This is demonstrated through analytical calculations and numerical simulations presented in the manuscript.

claim: The two power-law scaling regimes in the structure factor reflect the hexagonal geometry of small cell clusters and the uniaxial structure of global cellular flow.
source: Such a remarkable multiscale liquid crystal order leaves a distinct signature in the system's structure factor, which exhibits two different power-law scaling regimes, reflecting both the hexagonal geometry of small cells clusters and the uniaxial structure of the global cellular flow.
evidence: The manuscript provides theoretical interpretation linking the structure factor to underlying geometrical and flow properties.

claim: Multiscale order has been observed in layers of Madin-Darby canine kidney cells.
source: Our construction provides a theoretical framework to conceptualize the recent observation of multiscale order in layers of Madin–Darby canine kidney cells and pave the way for further theoretical developments.
evidence: This refers to recent experimental observations cited in the manuscript.

claim: Multicellular systems can move coherently within their micro-environment while retaining cell-cell contacts.
source: Whether spreading on a synthetic substrate (Serra-Picamal et al., 2012) or invading the extracellular matrix (Haeger et al., 2020), multicellular systems can move coherently within their micro-environment and coordinate the dynamics of their actin cytoskeleton, while retaining cell–cell contacts.
evidence: This is supported by cited experimental studies.

claim: Collective cell migration is instrumental for embryonic morphogenesis and wound healing.
source: This ability lies at the heart of a myriad of processes that are instrumental for life, such as embryonic morphogenesis and wound healing, but also of life-threatening conditions, such as metastatic cancer.
evidence: This is established biological knowledge.

claim: Collective cell migration is involved in metastatic cancer.
source: This ability lies at the heart of a myriad of processes that are instrumental for life, such as embryonic morphogenesis and wound healing, but also of life-threatening conditions, such as metastatic cancer.
evidence: This is established biological knowledge.

claim: Cell-resolved models have played a leading role in understanding collective cell migration.
source: Following the pioneering works by Honda, 1978; Nagai and Honda, 2001; Farhadifar et al., 2007; Bi et al., 2015; Bi et al., 2016, and others (Boromand et al., 2018; Mueller et al., 2019; Loewe et al., 2020; Monfared et al., 2021), cell-resolved models have played so far the leading role in this endeavour.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to pioneering works.

claim: Cell-resolved models portray confluent tissue as a collection of adjacent or overlapping polygonal cells.
source: Taking inspiration from the physics of foams (Graner et al., 2008; Marmottant et al., 2008), these models portray a confluent tissue as a collection of adjacent or overlapping polygonal cells (Figure 1a, b), whose dynamics is assumed to be governed by a set of overdamped Langevin equations, expressing the interplay between cells' autonomous motion and remodeling events, which change the local topology of the cellular networks.
evidence: This is described in the text and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Cell-resolved models agree remarkably well with experimental data on confluent monolayers.
source: Despite their conceptual simplicity, cell-resolved models agree remarkably well with experimental data on confluent monolayers (Park et al., 2015; Atia et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by cited experimental comparisons.

claim: Cell-resolved models account for a solid-to-liquid transition controlled by cell velocity and compliance to deformations.
source: In particular they account for a solid-to-liquid transition controlled by the cells velocity and their compliance to deformations (Bi et al., 2015; Bi et al., 2016; Loewe et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by cited modeling studies.

claim: The solid and isotropic liquid states of model-epithelia are separated by an intermediate hexatic phase.
source: Furthermore, as demonstrated by Pica Ciamarra and coworkers, the solid and isotropic liquid states of these model-epithelia are separated by an intermediate hexatic phase, in which the system exhibits the typical sixfold rotational symmetry of two-dimensional crystals and yet is able to flow (Li and Ciamarra, 2018; Pasupalak et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by cited computational studies.

claim: The hexatic phase exhibits sixfold rotational symmetry and is able to flow.
source: Furthermore, as demonstrated by Pica Ciamarra and coworkers, the solid and isotropic liquid states of these model-epithelia are separated by an intermediate hexatic phase, in which the system exhibits the typical sixfold rotational symmetry of two-dimensional crystals and yet is able to flow (Li and Ciamarra, 2018; Pasupalak et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by cited computational studies.

claim: Hexatic order has been recovered within the framework of the cellular Potts model.
source: Shortly after discovery, the same property has been recovered within the framework of the cellular Potts model, thereby strengthening the idea that hexatic order may in fact serve as a guiding principle to unravel the collective dynamics of confluent epithelia (Durand and Heu, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a cited study.

claim: In vitro studies of MDCK cell layers demonstrated that epithelial layers can feature both nematic and hexatic orders.
source: Furthermore, recent in vitro studies of Madin–Darby canine kidney (MDCK) cell layers demonstrated that epithelial layers can in fact feature both nematic and hexatic orders, with the former being dominant at large and the latter at short length scales (see Figure 1a, b and Armengol-Collado et al., 2023; Eckert et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by cited experimental studies and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Multiscale hexanematic order is believed to complement the complex network of regulatory pathways for multicellular organization.
source: This remarkable example of physical organization in biological matter, referred to as multiscale hexanematic order in Armengol-Collado et al., 2023, is believed to complement the complex network or regulatory pathways available to individual cells to achieve multicellular organization and select specific scale-dependent collective migration strategies.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on cited work.

claim: Previous theories of epithelial hydrodynamics are based on isotropic/polar/nematic active gels.
source: Previous theories of epithelial hydrodynamics can be schematically grouped in two categories: (1) models based on (isotropic/polar/nematic) active gels (Ranft et al., 2010; Popović et al., 2017; Pérez-González et al., 2019);
evidence: This categorizes existing literature with citations.

claim: Previous theories of epithelial hydrodynamics are built around the shape tensor.
source: (2) models built around the so-called shape tensor (Ishihara et al., 2017; Czajkowski et al., 2018; Hernandez and Marchetti, 2021; Grossman and Joanny, 2022), i.e. a rank-2 tensor, similar to the inertia tensor in kinematics, that embodies the geometrical structure of the polygonal cells.
evidence: This categorizes existing literature with citations.

claim: Previous hydrodynamic models can account at most for twofold rotational symmetry (nematic order).
source: Although both classes of models hold great heuristic value and represent a solid foundation for any future development, they suffer from the same limitation: being based on a tensorial order parameter whose rank is two or less, they can account at most for twofold rotational symmetry (i.e. nematic order), while leaving the small-scale hexatic order unresolved.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the mathematical structure of existing models.

claim: Previous hydrodynamic models leave small-scale hexatic order unresolved.
source: Although both classes of models hold great heuristic value and represent a solid foundation for any future development, they suffer from the same limitation: being based on a tensorial order parameter whose rank is two or less, they can account at most for twofold rotational symmetry (i.e. nematic order), while leaving the small-scale hexatic order unresolved.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the mathematical structure of existing models.

claim: Multiscale order is inherent to active liquid crystals with coupled order parameters.
source: We demonstrate that multiscale order is inherent to active liquid crystals with coupled order parameters, because of the indissoluble connection between shape and forces characterizing this class of non-equilibrium systems.
evidence: This is demonstrated through the theoretical framework developed in the manuscript.

claim: The indissoluble connection between shape and forces characterizes active liquid crystals with coupled order parameters.
source: We demonstrate that multiscale order is inherent to active liquid crystals with coupled order parameters, because of the indissoluble connection between shape and forces characterizing this class of non-equilibrium systems.
evidence: This is a theoretical insight from the hydrodynamic formulation.

claim: The structure factor exhibits two different power-law scaling regimes at small and large length scales.
source: Consistently with our linear analysis, both data sets exhibit two different power-law scaling regimes at small and large length scales.
evidence: This is demonstrated through numerical simulations of cell-resolved models.

claim: At large length scales, the structure factor scales like an inverse power law with exponent consistent with active nematics.
source: Conversely, at large length scales, the structure factor scales like an inverse power law, with exponent consistent with the large-scale behavior of active nematics (Chaté, 2020).
evidence: This is demonstrated through numerical simulations and comparison with known active nematic behavior.

claim: The cross-correlation function exhibits an oscillatory behavior at short distances in the active case.
source: In this case, the cross-correlation function exhibits an oscillatory behavior at short distances and vanishes at a length scale that becomes progressively large as the hexatic activity is increased.
evidence: This is demonstrated through numerical integration of the hydrodynamic equations.

claim: The cross-correlation function vanishes at a length scale that becomes progressively large as hexatic activity is increased.
source: In this case, the cross-correlation function exhibits an oscillatory behavior at short distances and vanishes at a length scale that becomes progressively large as the hexatic activity is increased.
evidence: This is demonstrated through numerical integration of the hydrodynamic equations.

claim: There exists a hierarchy of orientationally ordered structures nested into each other at different length scales.
source: Consistently with our previous analysis, this latter feature confirms the existence of a hierarchy of orientationally ordered structures nested into each other at different length scales.
evidence: This is inferred from the behavior of the cross-correlation function.

claim: Large-scale nematic order could arise from the self-organization of microscopic force hexapoles into force chains.
source: Whereas the origin of hexanematic order is still a matter of investigation, the current experimental and numerical evidence suggests that, similarly to granular materials (Majmudar and Behringer, 2005), large-scale nematic order could arise from the self-organization of the microscopic force hexapoles into force chains.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on analogy with granular materials.

claim: Linear arrays of cells simultaneously undergo apical constriction in the ventral furrow region during Drosophila gastrulation.
source: The possibility of similarity between these two phenomena has also been in relation to the initial phase of Drosophila gastrulation, where linear arrays of cells simultaneously undergo apical constriction in the ventral furrow region (Jason Gao et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a cited study on Drosophila development.

claim: Hexatic order may be relevant for short-scale remodeling events.
source: Although the consequences of such a remarkable versatility are yet to be explored, we expect hexatic order to be relevant for short-scale remodeling events, where the local nature of hexatic order, combined with the rich dynamics of hexatic defects (Zippelius et al., 1980; Amir and Nelson, 2012), may mediate processes such as cell intercalations and the rearrangement of multicellular rosettes (Blankenship et al., 2006; Rauzi, 2020).
evidence: This is a speculative prediction based on the properties of hexatic order.

claim: Hexatic order may mediate processes such as cell intercalations and the rearrangement of multicellular rosettes.
source: Although the consequences of such a remarkable versatility are yet to be explored, we expect hexatic order to be relevant for short-scale remodeling events, where the local nature of hexatic order, combined with the rich dynamics of hexatic defects (Zippelius et al., 1980; Amir and Nelson, 2012), may mediate processes such as cell intercalations and the rearrangement of multicellular rosettes (Blankenship et al., 2006; Rauzi, 2020).
evidence: This is a speculative prediction based on the properties of hexatic order.

claim: Local motion may be coordinated at the large scale by underlying nematic order.
source: Such a local motion, in turn, may be coordianted at the large scale by the underlying nematic order, giving rise to a persistent unidirectional flow, such as that observed during wound healing and cancer progression (Friedl and Gilmour, 2009).
evidence: This is a speculative prediction about how multiscale order coordinates cellular behavior.

claim: The epithelial and mesenchymal states represent the two ends of a spectrum of intermediate phenotypes.
source: Furthermore, the existence of multiscale liquid crystal order echoes the most recent understanding of phenotypic plasticity in tissues, according to which the epithelial (i.e. solid-like) and mesenchymal (i.e. liquid-like) states represent the two ends of a spectrum of intermediate phenotypes (Zhang and Weinberg, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a cited review on phenotypic plasticity.

claim: Intermediate phenotypes display distinctive cellular characteristics including adhesion, motility, stemness, and invasiveness.
source: These intermediate states display distinctive cellular characteristics, including adhesion, motility, stemness and, in the case of cancer cells, invasiveness, drug resistance, etc.
evidence: This is established knowledge about epithelial-mesenchymal transition states.

source: The first term on the right-hand side of Equation 3 is the stress resulting from the contractile or extensile forces exerted at the length scale of individual cells.

source: The former is the well-known active nematic length scale, dictating both the hydrodynamic stability (Voituriez et al., 2005) and the large-scale structure of spatiotemporal chaos in active nematics (Giomi, 2015) and whose signature in multicellular systems has been identified in both eukaryotes (Blanch-Mercader et al., 2018) and prokaryotes (You et al., 2018).
